description: Bootstrap three real Peers, elect node 1 using ticks and generated votes, persist/apply the prefix, then admit A from node 2 and B from node 3 while losing A heartbeat replies. Release B replies after the pending queue contains both requests. Observe each raw emitted response and follower ReadyToRead using destination as identity, independently of context being compared.

semantic_changes: Replaces actual networking and disk I/O with a deterministic FIFO message queue and the existing TestLogDB; executes unchanged Peer and raft code.
Observes private queue state only for admission prerequisites; reads output after synchronous ownership returns.
No production source, predicates or protocol state transitions are modified.

legality.derivation: Launch uses real initial bootstrap configuration entries; the driver persists each Peer Update in the captured TestLogDB, applies bootstrap changes/no-op entries in order, calls Commit and NotifyRaftLastApplied, and dispatches every surviving wire message through Peer.Handle. Only node 1 receives election ticks until a real election and current-term no-op commit complete. No role, vote, commit, match, pending-read or handler is injected. All peers are caught up before reads. The predetermined transport policy drops both replies for context A; it temporarily holds B replies at queue head until both admissions are sampled, then drains FIFO. Transport send failures in the captured implementation establish message loss as a supported condition. Persisting Replicate before delivery is a permitted stronger ordering. Fixed context values are distinct admissible outputs of the nonzero context generator, not results selected after execution. Application contains only bootstrap membership entries and the empty leader no-op, so the driver has no client command semantics to replace. All work is synchronous in one test goroutine, with no background worker or resource cleanup debt.
legality.applicability: One package-local three-node Peer history with in-memory persistence and no crashes. A loses replies; B confirmation remains actual target-generated traffic. Observation ends after all surviving messages and Update outputs are consumed.
unresolved: Formal execution and current correspondence review have not occurred.
alternatives: Directly invoking confirm or synthesizing heartbeat acknowledgements would not establish the required legal history and is not used.

grounding.derivation: The queue test explicitly expects distinct original contexts in the returned prefix. node.handleReadIndex registers a batch under its supplied SystemCtx, and pendingReadIndex.addReady uses exact equality to find that batch. Therefore the forwarding handoff must preserve that identity for each response it produces. This local composed interface duty does not require a successful-read deadline or infer a stale application read.
grounding.applicability: Distinct nonzero contexts, fixed three-full-voter membership, a leader with a committed current-term entry, and a completed confirmation of multiple pending forwarded requests. No Byzantine sender or crash.
alternatives: A single returned status or local requester does not exercise the remote coalesced-prefix discrepancy.
Caller timeout can terminate a request but cannot turn another request context into its identity.

observable_properties.description: For each independently identified requesting origin, the response full SystemCtx equals the admitted request full SystemCtx. Missing or ambiguous responses are unknown, not observed falsity or holds.

uncertainties: The receiving ReadyToRead context/index are diagnostic output; the sole predicate compares complete wire context strings to admitted contexts.
Does not execute NodeHost caller completion or demonstrate a later stale read.
Source-grounded local trial observations are construction knowledge only; the trusted runner must execute these fixed bytes.
